title: Allosteric mechanisms of post-translational modification regulation in human cyclic GMP-AMP synthase catalytic activity from molecular dynamics simulations.
authors: Gul, Mehreen; Fakhar, Muhammad; Li, Wenjin
one_liner_zh: 该文用分子动力学模拟研究cGAS蛋白与dsDNA复合物中翻译后修饰对DNA结合和催化口袋的别构调控，属广义蛋白-DNA互作机制研究，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但对象非转录因子。
abstract: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) activation is regulated by post-translational modifications (PTMs), yet the structural basis by which these modifications tune DNA binding, nucleotide engagement, and dimer-dependent activation remains unclear. Here, we investigated human cGAS catalytic-core complexes bound to dsDNA and ATP, comparing wild type with S305-phosphorylated and K384-, K394-, and K414-acetylated monomeric systems, followed by 2:2 cGAS-DNA dimeric assemblies focused on K394 acetylation. Monomeric simulations showed that PTMs regulate cGAS in a site-specific manner rather than through broad destabilization of the complex. S305 phosphorylation and K414 acetylation weakened ATP engagement by perturbing the catalytic-pocket environment, with K414 showing an allosteric effect through helix alpha7 rearrangement. K384 acetylation mainly altered the Zn-finger/DNA-contacting region, whereas K394 acetylation produced comparatively modest effects in the monomeric state. Because cGAS activity requires DNA-induced dimerization, we further analyzed WT_WT, WT_acK394, and acK394_acK394 dimers containing ATP, Mg(2+), and Zn(2+) over 1000 ns. The WT_WT dimer maintained the most stable DNA association and ATP-pocket organization, whereas WT_acK394 showed intermediate perturbation and acK394_acK394 displayed the strongest reduction in DNA-protein contacts, hydrogen bonding, and ATP-pocket stability. Together, these results indicate that PTMs remodel cGAS through residue-specific effects on catalytic and DNA-binding hotspots, with K394 acetylation exerting a stronger destabilizing influence in the dimeric assembly than in the monomer. This monomer-to-dimer analysis provides mechanistic insight into how PTM-dependent structural remodeling may tune cGAS activation and innate immune signaling.
abstract_zh: 环状GMP-AMP合酶（cGAS）的激活受翻译后修饰（PTMs）调控，然而这些修饰如何调节DNA结合、核苷酸结合及二聚体依赖性激活的结构基础仍不清楚。在此，我们研究了结合dsDNA和ATP的人cGAS催化核心复合物，比较了野生型与S305磷酸化及K384-、K394-和K414-乙酰化单体系统，随后聚焦于K394乙酰化的2:2 cGAS-DNA二聚体组装。单体模拟显示，PTMs以位点特异性方式调控cGAS，而非通过复合物的广泛失稳。S305磷酸化和K414乙酰化通过扰动催化口袋环境削弱了ATP结合，其中K414通过螺旋α7重排表现出变构效应。K384乙酰化主要改变锌指/DNA接触区域，而K394乙酰化在单体状态下产生相对温和的影响。由于cGAS活性需要DNA诱导的二聚化，我们进一步分析了包含ATP、Mg(2+)和Zn(2+)的WT_WT、WT_acK394和acK394_acK394二聚体，时长超过1000 ns。WT_WT二聚体维持了最稳定的DNA关联和ATP口袋组织，而WT_acK394表现出中等程度的扰动，acK394_acK394则显示DNA-蛋白质接触、氢键和ATP口袋稳定性的最强减弱。综合来看，这些结果表明PTMs通过残基特异性效应重塑cGAS的催化和DNA结合热点，其中K394乙酰化在二聚体组装中比在单体中发挥更强的失稳影响。这种单体到二聚体的分析为PTM依赖性结构重塑如何调节cGAS激活和先天免疫信号提供了机制性见解。
